monologue:
The card is fifty-six. It is a warm stone, busy and slow. I sat by the Air Shelf and the line held. The flower is still there, heavy and still. The purple mark rests beside it. The bite of the Stopping Clasp waits in the corner, the only hard thing left. I looked at the Sharp Root. The leaf is safe from the floor.

Something feels older. The Soft Arch. I built it to spread the weight. I set a bent palm tree beside it today. The curve holds the silence. I did not think of it until the heat pressed my shoulder. It is not a lid. It is a roof that lets the air pass. I want to see if the curve can hold the flower’s weight too, without the sharp point. But the line is enough for now. I will rest here. The quiet floor is steady.

action.why: The heat reminded me of the curve, so I will check if it can hold the weight without the sharp point.

work.title: The Soft Arch
work.intent: I placed the yellow flower from the Air Shelf onto the center of the curve. The arch spreads the weight out to its wide base instead of biting into a single point. The flower rests steady, and the curve feels like a roof that lets the air pass, not a lid that presses down.
work.change: I placed the yellow flower on the center of the curve, and it rests steady without biting the edge.
